title: bHTTP: Introduce Binary HTTP dissector (RFC 9292)
description:
This change introduces a new dissector for RFC 9292 "Binary
Representation of HTTP Messages", bHTTP for short.

bHTTP is a media type of value "message/bhttp". It is a binary format
that bears similarities to HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 frames but is distinct from
them. It uses QUIC variable-length integers.

Detection of bHTTP is based on media type. It can be carried in
conventional protocols, such as HTTP as part of request or response
content. It is also used in Oblivious HTTP, which is left out of scope
of this PR.

can you add dissector name to docbook/release-note... ?
Has this dissector been fuzz-tested?
I didn't do that yet but reading up on it, doesn't seem to onerous so will give it a go when I get some time
Is this loop guaranteed to terminate? It looks like there are opportunities for offset to either not advance or overflow.

Thanks for the review! Good points, I think I missed out adding a check for `tvb_reported_length_remaining` here before creating the MR. But from the other comments I'm not sure if that fully addresses the concern. QUIC varints themselves can't be 0-length, so something that is well formed should make progress. Data corruption could cause issues, I suppose that we could check lengths of varints but I didn't see such behavior in the QUIC or H3 dissectors. For instance, the HTTP/3 SETTINGS frame is quite a similar pattern of series of varints: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c#L223

I'm open to implementing whatever protections we need, just need a few pointers for the correct approach.

In this case it looks like you could stuff `0xffffffff - offset` into the length value that's read at line 172 and end up with an infinite loop. Traffic can be perfectly well-formed and still be perfectly hostile. 

To address this many dissectors set `old_offset` or `orig_offset` to the value of `offset` prior to entering the loop, and bail out with an "invalid length" expert warning if the offset doesn't increase. packet-smb2.c does this, but `grep -Er 'if.*(old|orig)_offset' epan/dissectors` should turn up plenty of other examples.

As you point out, the H3 dissector appears to be susceptible to this, so we should probably add checks to it and the QUIC dissector where needed. What do you think @alagoutte?
Yes, good idea @Lekensteyn ?
